### Bruns 2020 NBS2 borosilicate experimental candidate

The review-only packet `experimental/material-batches/bruns-nbs2-borosilicate-20261023`
uses selected facts from Sebastian Bruns, Tobias Uesbeck, Dominik Weil,
Doris Möncke, Leo van Wüllen, Karsten Durst and Dominique de Ligny (2020),
*Influence of Al2O3 Addition on Structure and Mechanical Properties of
Borosilicate Glasses*, Frontiers in Materials 7:189,
[DOI 10.3389/fmats.2020.00189](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmats.2020.00189).
Copyright 2020 the authors. The article-specific notice on PDF p.14 and the
[publisher article](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/materials/articles/10.3389/fmats.2020.00189/full)
identify the [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

Changes consist of selected nominal and separately qualified ICP-OES oxide
composition facts from Table 1, four furnace-cooled density means/SDs from
Table 3, supporting preparation/method facts and original curation notes.
No endorsement by the authors or publisher is implied. No separate third-party
credit appears in the inspected selected table captions or density passage;
this scope does not extend to referenced works or other credited content.
The source PDF, page images, full text, figures and raw measurements are not
bundled or relicensed under the project MIT license. The reviewed publisher
PDF SHA-256 is `c6268f9f14320e9355bfe04bf02f47eb3d7ca00e30c7281a16fd3b1289913da6`.
These are source-level transcription and rights checks, not legal clearance,
experimental replication or independent scientific approval.

### Historical Ultimaker Nylon family and product-identifier references

The existing Zenodo 8089569 Nylon candidate uses two jointly required, manufacturer-authored documents hosted by third parties. They provide narrowly scoped historical identity context for `mat_aniskevich_2023_ultimaker_nylon`; the separately attributed study remains the source of measured properties.

- `ultimaker_nylon_sds_20190114`: Ultimaker B.V., *Nylon Safety Data Sheet*, version 4.002, dated January 14, 2019. [Source hosted by MatterHackers](https://www.matterhackers.com/r/vq1Soq). Selected PDF pages 1, 3 and 5 identify the manufacturer product family as a polyamide grade based on PA6/PA66, include transparent and black colors, and establish the document revision. Reviewed original: **78,202 bytes**; SHA-256 `a25c0275486ca9639fc89ee6a351d29e6e34d0938fa936bf10a9b8e2c42c2863`. Frozen source-record canonical SHA-256: `7f41012eeff777e0d0b3e6a5d69b2846cfc1e8d5d78bb0e5f0dedeca71e7a0fa`.
- `ultimaker_nylon_pricing_20210504`: Ultimaker USA, Inc., *New York State bidder pricing document, solicitation 23185, Attachment 1*, printed date May 4, 2021 (`5/4/2021`; PDF creation metadata also dates it to 2021-05-04). No separate version number is asserted. [Source hosted by New York State OGS](https://online.ogs.ny.gov/purchase/spg/pdfdocs/2310623185PL_Ultimaker.pdf). Selected PDF pages 1, 3 and 4 establish bidder attribution, table columns and the transparent Nylon row: `1647` appears in both the bidder-stock and manufacturer-part-number columns. `M2085` is a description-field token, not a verified chemical grade. Reviewed original: **233,996 bytes**; SHA-256 `113a0e9157044000a08311bd0d10081ae81fa045197812d41f9393d167d3d1cc`. Frozen source-record canonical SHA-256: `02f1733f3a8cabf27b0f567e238675393c3b8ecff8cd84bec2767ed350a54ba2`.

Canonical source-record hashes use UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, `ensure_ascii=False`, and no trailing newline. Document byte hashes identify the actual reviewed PDFs; source-record hashes identify the frozen curated records.

The historical family fact and product-code correspondence support identity qualification only. They do not authenticate the studied lot, its manufacture date or composition, formula continuity, PA6:PA66 ratio, molecular architecture, purity or an exact chemical grade. The measured reference-filament state's composition remains unknown. Colors do not create separate identities, and these references do not add a black measured state. The pricing description's `750` token has no explicit mass unit, so no package mass is imported. No 2017 SDS is relied upon, and no manufacturer numerical properties or prices are imported.

No explicit open reuse license was verified for either manufacturer-authored document. Third-party hosting, including government hosting, does not establish a public-domain status or asset reuse permission. The separate Zenodo dataset's CC BY 4.0 license and this repository's MIT license are not inherited by these documents. The distributed curation is limited to sparse attributed identity facts, bibliographic metadata, hashes and original qualification notes; original PDFs, rendered pages and full extracted text remain external review evidence and are not bundled. This limited factual curation does not assert broader reuse rights or legal clearance.

## Selected Tough PLA constituent context (2026-10-21)

Ultimaker, *Tough PLA Safety Data Sheet*, SDS ID UM00009, version 2.0,
revised 2022-12-22 (superseding 2019-01-14),
[official manufacturer SDS](https://um-support-files.ultimaker.com/materials/2.85mm/sds/TOUGH-PLA/UM_Tough%20PLA_EU_en_SDSv2.0.pdf).
The date identifies the document revision, not the experiment or original
publication. PDF page 1, section 1.1, covers Tough PLA Black and White;
page 2, section 3.2, names PLA and an unspecified acrylic polymer.

Only sparse constituent/product-family classification facts and original
qualification notes are included. The manufacturer information supports one
source-qualified Tough PLA identity; the two colors retain their separate
workbook measurements. The SDS does not verify the workbook codes `20231`
or `202300` as manufacturer SKUs or certify the tested lots. No PMMA,
constituent fraction, ingredient function or complete formulation is inferred.

No explicit open reuse license was verified for this SDS. The raw PDF,
rendered pages and full extracted text are excluded. The Zenodo dataset's
CC BY 4.0 license applies separately and does not license this manufacturer
document. No blanket source-asset reuse, project MIT relicensing or legal
clearance is asserted. The reviewed PDF is 496191 bytes, SHA-256
`3b97d600b92f44da56a4c5c8bae029dddbc4b2d400d3c7501cafed9b7aaf69cf`.

## Selected Zenodo reference-filament facts (2026-10-21)

Aniskevich Andrey and Bulderberga Olga (creator names as deposited),
*Characterisation of mechanical properties of materials used in 3D printing*,
Zenodo, 2023-06-28. [Version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8089569](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8089569);
[concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8089568](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8089568).
The official Zenodo version metadata and DataCite concept metadata identify
[Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
The concept and version identifiers refer to one dataset.

Selected facts come from `Annex 3.1. Characterisation of mechanical properties.xlsx`
(1391320 bytes, MD5 `c4842898d2c389ccd7a902691d8a4fa3`, SHA-256
`830b2c9277dcc2d03265b63e311a5e7089c258ebb6a389b45d07601ae4b2e4e7`).
The retained scope is the selected reference-filament measurements, identity
locators and applicable source qualifications. Adaptations consist of structured
transcription, authored interface names and original scope notes; source numeric
values and units are preserved. The raw workbook, full worksheets, source
images, drawings and extended source text are excluded. Source content is not
relicensed under project MIT, and no source endorsement is asserted.

Three separate manufacturer sources support constituent classification only:

- ProtoPlant / Protopasta, [Conductive PLA FAQ](https://proto-pasta.com/pages/conductive-pla),
  supports the PLA/dispersant/conductive-carbon-black description. Selected
  indexed official-page text was inspected; direct retrieval returned HTTP 429,
  so no original-byte hash or page revision date is claimed.
- Add North, [Product catalogue 2022](https://storage.googleapis.com/addnorth-com-public/catalog/addnorth_product_catalogue_2022.pdf),
  PDF page 19 / printed page 37, supports graphene in Koltron G1. The study
  workbook separately identifies its PVDF polymer. The adjacent Adamant S1
  description and its purity statement are excluded.
- MakerBot / Stratasys, [MakerBot Launches METHOD Materials Development Program](https://investors.stratasys.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/537/makerbot-launches-method-materials-development-program),
  2019-11-19, identifies carbon nanotubes in the named KIMYA ABS ESD product.
  This historical manufacturer-platform partner statement is not a tested-lot
  composition assay, and equivalence across product revisions is not asserted.

No explicit open reuse license was verified for these three manufacturer
sources. Only sparse attributed constituent facts, exact locators and original
qualification notes are included. No manufacturer pages, PDFs, images, tables,
extended prose, numerical properties, filler fractions or complete formulations
are bundled or inferred. The dataset's CC BY 4.0 license does not cover these
separate sources. Limited factual curation does not assert blanket reuse rights
or legal clearance.

The bounded [Bruns NBS2 borosilicate increment](experimental/material-batches/bruns-nbs2-borosilicate-20261023/INTEGRATION.md) adds four nominal oxide recipes with one furnace-cooled density mean and SD each. Nominal and ICP-OES compositions remain separate; exact independent n and density-test temperature are unknown, and the 4.0 mol% sample retains its crucible-cooling exception. No quenched state creates another identity.

The bounded [Nylon historical-identity follow-up](experimental/material-batches/zenodo-8089569-nylon-followup-20261021/README.md) records one source-qualified historical manufacturer family and its separately measured transparent-filament state. The historical documents do not establish the studied lot, formula continuity, ratio or molecular architecture.

The bounded [Tough PLA identity follow-up](experimental/material-batches/zenodo-8089569-tough-pla-followup-20261021/README.md) records the reconsideration of two color rows as one source-qualified identity. The [original batch evidence availability note](experimental/material-batches/zenodo-8089569-filaments-20261021/EVIDENCE_AVAILABILITY.md) clarifies which finite-review artifacts remain local-only.
